# Boiler Service 2023

## Summary

The annual service took place on 18 September 2023, booked with the firm that has looked after the boiler since it was fitted. The engineer was on site for about an hour, working through the unit from the top down with the case off and a mat on the floor for the panels. He started with the flue and the combustion readings, then moved to the water side and the condensate, and finished by checking the seals around the case before he put anything back. Everything he measured went onto the benchmark sheet, which he signed and dated before handing it to me. The reminder card went back inside the door on his way out, so the next visit is already pencilled in for the same month next year. I asked a few questions about the noise the boiler makes when it starts and he said it was normal for the model. The whole visit cost what the quote said it would, and I paid on the day by card. The card has the date for next autumn written on it, and the folder by the meter now holds this sheet alongside the earlier ones, which makes a useful record of how the unit has behaved year by year.

## Findings

The condensate trap was blocked, which was the main fault of the visit and the likely cause of the gurgling I had been hearing when the boiler fired. The trap had collected grit and a slimy deposit that had narrowed the outlet until water was backing up rather than draining away. The gas rate was checked at 9.2 kW against the figure on the benchmark sheet, and it sat close enough to the specification that no adjustment was needed. The flame picture was clean and steady through the sight glass, with no lifting or yellowing at the burner. The magnetic filter on the return had a thin layer of black sludge on the magnet, which he cleaned and refitted with new washers. The case seals were intact and still soft, so none of them needed replacing this year. There was no sign of weeping at the pipework he could reach, and the flue readings were within the range he expected for the unit. The condensate was the only thing out of sorts, and he said everything else was where he would want it on a unit of this age. He noted the trap as the likely cause of the noise and asked me to listen for it again once the heating was back in daily use. He said the trap would want checking again at the next service rather than being replaced now.

## Actions

He flushed the condensate trap with hot water and worked a short length of wire through the outlet until it ran clear, then refitted it and poured water through to prove the drain. A dose of inhibitor went into the system through the filling loop and he told me to leave the heating to run for a day before bleeding anything. He also told me to bleed the hall radiator once things had warmed up, since it had been cool at the top for a week or two and was probably holding air. The filter was cleaned and refitted, the case went back on with all its screws, and the benchmark sheet went into the folder by the meter. The next visit was booked for the following autumn, and he said to ring sooner if the pressure on the gauge started to fall. He left a short written note of what he had done, which I filed with the benchmark sheet.
